record.paper_title: Major Unsolved Problems in Space Plasma Physics
record.original_question: What physical mechanism heats the solar corona from chromospheric temperatures of thousands of kelvin to more than one million kelvin, and how does that mechanism determine the speed and temperature of the solar wind, especially the fast wind above coronal holes, given that fluid models require additional heat sources and proposed mechanisms such as Alfven-wave damping, reconnection events, and velocity filtration each face observational or theoretical constraints?

evidence.quote: Exactly how the corona is heated is not understood
the heating mechanism determines both the speed and temperature of the solar wind, especially the fast wind above coronal holes.
Determining how the corona and solar wind are heated and accelerated continues to be a challenging unsolved problem.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
The solar chromosphere has temperatures of order a few thousand kelvin, yet the overlying solar corona reaches temperatures in excess of 10^6 K, and a fast solar wind (with speeds of roughly 700–800 km/s near 1 AU) emerges from coronal holes. Standard fluid (hydrodynamic) models of the corona and solar wind, based purely on thermal conduction and pressure gradients, cannot reproduce these observed temperatures and outflow speeds without invoking additional, extended sources of energy and momentum deposition.

Identify and quantitatively characterize the physical mechanism(s) responsible for:

(a) heating the plasma from chromospheric temperatures (~10^3–10^4 K) to coronal temperatures (>10^6 K) against radiative and conductive losses, and

(b) accelerating the solar wind, in particular the fast wind streams above coronal holes, determining its asymptotic speed, temperature, and species-dependent properties (ion vs. electron temperatures, temperature anisotropies, differential streaming).

Specifically, determine which of the candidate mechanisms—including but not limited to (i) damping of Alfvén waves and turbulent cascades of MHD/kinetic Alfvén waves, (ii) magnetic reconnection events (nanoflares, jets, interchange reconnection at coronal-hole boundaries), and (iii) velocity filtration of suprathermal particle distributions—operates, in what proportions, and on what spatial and temporal scales, in a way consistent with all observational constraints (spectroscopic line widths and intensities, in situ plasma and field measurements, particle distribution functions) and theoretical requirements (energy budget, wave generation and dissipation rates, plasma stability).
artifact.category_tag: Coronal heating and solar wind acceleration
artifact.status_search_result: The coronal heating and solar wind acceleration problem remains an active open question in space plasma physics. Recent Parker Solar Probe results (including 2025 work on a "helicity barrier" in Alfvénic turbulence and on ambipolar-electric-potential-driven acceleration) provide significant new evidence and partial mechanisms, but no single mechanism has been established as the complete explanation, and multiple candidate mechanisms (Alfvén-wave/turbulence damping, reconnection-driven heating, kinetic effects) continue to be investigated.

status_evidence.title: New Insights into Coronal Heating and Solar Wind Acceleration
status_evidence.snippet: A recent study presented evidence for a newly discovered helicity barrier that helps answer long-standing questions about coronal heating and solar wind acceleration.
status_evidence.claim: Recent (2025) discoveries provide partial new evidence but the problem is still being actively investigated.

status_evidence.title: A kinetic model of solar wind acceleration driven by ambipolar electric potential and velocity-space diffusion
status_evidence.snippet: Parker Solar Probe observations have revealed that most of the solar wind acceleration occurs very close to the Sun... the exact mechanism accounting for the remaining acceleration has not yet been identified.
status_evidence.claim: As of 2025 the full acceleration mechanism remains unidentified.

status_evidence.title: Heating Mechanisms and Radio Response from the Solar Chromosphere to Corona
status_evidence.snippet: Active research on heating mechanisms continues into 2025-2026.
status_evidence.claim: Coronal heating mechanisms remain an open research area.
